# Phase 1b-i's class x chain gate: the English label expected for each
# deinflection chain the v2 table generates.
# Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-02-engine-v2-phase1b-i-design.md §3-§4.
#
# Columns, tab-separated: surface, chain, expected.
#   surface  - a complete conjugated word. Table::chains_ending_at does not
#              consult the dictionary, so the headword only serves the reader.
#   chain    - space-separated steps, innermost first: class:form for the
#              first step, lemma:form for each auxiliary after it. Class and
#              form names are table_data.rs's IPADIC names; lemmas are
#              table.rs's ATTACHES_TO spellings.
#   expected - the label, or "-" for None.
#
# The English column was written by hand from "Japanese verb conjugation",
# English Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_verb_conjugation),
# read 2026-09, terminology only, in the learner-standard register the design
# fixes: Causative, Passive/Potential, Negative, Volitional, Polite, Want-to,
# Past, Te-form, Copula, Conditional, Imperative, Adverbial. It was written
# before crates/jparser/src/engine/label.rs existed, and is authoritative over
# it. assets/conjugations.json, src/conjugation.rs and src/matcher/
# (matcher.rs and matcher/verb.rs) were not opened while this file was
# written. Those four paths were deleted at Phase 1b-ii and are recoverable
# from git history; they are named here because naming what was not read is
# the attestation.
#
# Rows marked "table finding" are surfaces that are not natural Japanese but
# are chains the table generates today. They are labelled by the same rules;
# the cause is an ATTACHES_TO row (span shape, Phase 1a's territory) and is
# recorded in the 1b-i handoff, not fixed here.
#
# A surface can appear twice with different chains (書け is both 仮定形 and
# 命令ｅ). Each chain is its own row.

# --- Part A: depth 0. One row per (adjective?, form) reachable from a class
# --- JMDICT_POS_CLASS maps. Only Conditional, Imperative and Adverbial name a
# --- form on its own; every other form is the plain form or a dangling stem.
書け	五段・カ行イ音便:仮定形	Conditional

書いたら	五段・カ行イ音便:連用タ接続 た:仮定形	Conditional
書いた	五段・カ行イ音便:連用タ接続 た:基本形	Past
書いたろ	五段・カ行イ音便:連用タ接続 た:未然形	Past
# The voiced past だ is 特殊・タ, the class of た, which is what IPADIC tags
# 読ん|だ and 読ん|だら as. Until 2026-09-23 ATTACHES_TO pointed it at the
# copula class 特殊・ダ, whose forms are なら/な/なれ/だ/だろ/だっ/で, and this
# block recorded that as a table finding: 読んだら was unreachable, and the
# rows 読んなら, 読んな, 読んなれ, 読んだっ and a second 読んで were spurious.
# Those five were removed with the fix, not quietly; 読んだら replaces the
# first.
読んだら	五段・マ行:連用タ接続 だ:仮定形	Conditional
読んだ	五段・マ行:連用タ接続 だ:基本形	Past
読んだろ	五段・マ行:連用タ接続 だ:未然形	Past
書いて	五段・カ行イ音便:連用タ接続 て:基本形	Te-form
読んで	五段・マ行:連用タ接続 で:基本形	Te-form
# です attaches to 基本形, so its depth-1 surfaces read as nonstandard
# Japanese on an ichidan verb (食べるです). They are the chains the table
# generates for the lemma.
# 食べるでしょ (です:未然形) was a row here until 2026-09-23, when table.rs
# blocked that form: nothing could follow it, so it only ever left a lone う
# behind 〜でしょう. Removed with the block, not quietly.
食べるです	一段:基本形 です:基本形	Polite
食べるでし	一段:基本形 です:連用形	Polite
# The six じゃ/や rows that followed (食べるじゃ, 食べるじゃろ, 食べるじゃっ,
# 食べるや, 食べるやろ, 食べるやっ) went with those ATTACHES_TO rows on
# 2026-09-23: they fired on real text after every 基本形, the te-form's て
# included (そうやって as 沿う Copula Te-form), so they were removed, not
# quietly.

# --- Part C: curated, depth 2-6. Every override and the Polite dedup, the
# --- corpus's deepest chain, and one row per remaining mapped class. An
# --- auxiliary's form here is the one the next auxiliary's ATTACHES_TO row
# --- requires (られ before ます is 連用形; before ない it is 未然形).

読みたかった	五段・マ行:連用形 たい:連用タ接続 た:基本形	Want-to Past
# The dedup and step-order rules, pinned on chains that are not ます+です.
# A formatter that special-cased "です after ます says Polite once" instead of
# deduplicating generically would pass every row above and still double a word
# on the two causative/passive stacks below. 食べたです is the only row where a
# word-contributing auxiliary is followed by another, so it is what pins
# "auxiliary words in step order" rather than "Past comes last".
書かせさせる	五段・カ行イ音便:未然形 せる:未然形 させる:基本形	Causative
書かれられる	五段・カ行イ音便:未然形 れる:未然形 られる:基本形	Passive/Potential
食べたです	一段:連用形 た:基本形 です:基本形	Past Polite

# 書い, 行っ and 高かっ — the three bare 連用タ接続 stems — had a row each
# here until table.rs's BOUND_FORMS stopped the table generating them as
# whole words. They are still generated under た/て/だ/で/ちゃう, which is the
# only place they occur: 書いた and 高かった below still have their rows.
#
# ちゃう/じゃう and the ちまう/じまう they contract from are the てしまう
# auxiliary: the action is carried through, often with regret. "Completive" is
# the one word below that the Wikipedia terminology list above does not carry
# — that article names the construction but not a one-word English gloss for
# it. The word is the standard grammatical term for the aspect (Wikipedia,
# "Grammatical aspect", read 2026-09), chosen over "Regrettably" because the
# regret reading is the secondary one and the parser cannot tell them apart,
# the same reason れる/られる are labelled "Passive/Potential".
# 未然ウ接続 and 未然形 rows are stems, not free words, listed for the same
# reason 書いたろ is: the walk reaches them and every reachable tuple needs a
# row.
# 待ってよ and 遊んでよ had a row each here for てる/でる's 命令ｙｏ and
# 未然ウ接続 until table.rs's AUX_FORM_BLOCK stopped the table generating
# the よ surface at all. The contraction's imperative is 待ってろ, never
# 待ってよ, and the surface collided with the sentence-final particle よ --
# 22 absorbed particles over 8,334 lines of dialogue, five of them the
# 忘れないでよ shape that destroyed the negation outright. Named here
# rather than quietly dropped, the way the three 連用タ接続 stems above
# are.
#
# ている/でいる are the uncontracted form of the same auxiliary, added
# 2026-09-18 so that 待っていた stops reading 待って | い | た with い glossed
# "the Boar (twelfth sign of the Chinese zodiac)" -- 218 corpus sentences,
# the largest single count the disagreement probe found. Same 一段 class and
# 一段 class. **The two よ-forms are NOT blocked here**, unlike てる below:
# てる's てよ collides with the sentence-final particle because 待って is a
# word and よ is a particle, but ていよ cannot decompose that way -- 待ってい
# is not a standalone anything. Blocking them by analogy cost 待っていよう and
# 遊んでいよう, which are ordinary Japanese; measured over 8,334 lines,
# unblocking them changes 2 sentences, both gains, and absorbs no particle.
# The stem てい is what reaches た and ます: 待っていた, 待っています.
待っていれ	五段・タ行:連用タ接続 ている:仮定形	Progressive Conditional
待っていよ	五段・タ行:連用タ接続 ている:命令ｙｏ	Progressive Imperative
待っていよ	五段・タ行:連用タ接続 ている:未然ウ接続	Progressive
遊んでいよ	五段・バ行:連用タ接続 でいる:命令ｙｏ	Progressive Imperative
遊んでいよ	五段・バ行:連用タ接続 でいる:未然ウ接続	Progressive
待っていりゃ	五段・タ行:連用タ接続 ている:仮定縮約１	Progressive Conditional
待っていん	五段・タ行:連用タ接続 ている:体言接続特殊	Progressive
待っていろ	五段・タ行:連用タ接続 ている:命令ｒｏ	Progressive Imperative
待っている	五段・タ行:連用タ接続 ている:基本形	Progressive
待ってい	五段・タ行:連用タ接続 ている:未然形	Progressive
待ってい	五段・タ行:連用タ接続 ている:連用形	Progressive
遊んでいれ	五段・バ行:連用タ接続 でいる:仮定形	Progressive Conditional
遊んでいりゃ	五段・バ行:連用タ接続 でいる:仮定縮約１	Progressive Conditional
遊んでいん	五段・バ行:連用タ接続 でいる:体言接続特殊	Progressive
遊んでいろ	五段・バ行:連用タ接続 でいる:命令ｒｏ	Progressive Imperative
遊んでいる	五段・バ行:連用タ接続 でいる:基本形	Progressive
遊んでい	五段・バ行:連用タ接続 でいる:未然形	Progressive
遊んでい	五段・バ行:連用タ接続 でいる:連用形	Progressive
#
# ていく/でいく are the directional auxiliary, added 2026-09-18 so that
# 引きずっていった stops reading 引きずって | いった and 歩いていく stops
# reading 歩いて | いく. Measured over three visual-novel corpora, 75,767
# sentences, 1,189 lines carry one -- 9.6 to 17.3 per *thousand* in each of
# the three, so it is a rate rather than one writer's habit. It is the most
# frequent 〜て auxiliary still split, not the only one: 〜てくる, 〜ておく and
# 〜てみる have no rows either.
#
# 五段・カ行促音便 is 行く's own class and gives the whole paradigm from one
# row per voicing: ていく, ていっ(た), ていか(ない), ていき(ます), ていけ(ば),
# ていこ(う). でいく mirrors でいる and follows an onbin stem only.
#
# "Directional" is the THIRD word in this file the header's Wikipedia
# terminology list does not carry. That article has no one-word gloss for
# 〜ていく, and JMdict has no ていく headword either, so neither of the two
# precedents above applies: Completive took the standard aspect term and
# Progressive took the aspect term with JMdict's own gloss agreeing. This one
# takes the learner-standard name instead -- 〜ていく and 〜てくる are taught as
# the directional pair, motion away from and toward the speaker. It is
# unqualified for the Completive reason: the two readings, spatial (歩いていく)
# and temporal (増えていく), are not balanced enough to warrant a slash the way
# Passive/Potential is. It cannot be confused with a form name here, which
# "Continuative" would be -- Wikipedia uses that only as an alias for 連用形.
# **One thing to settle before 〜てくる gets rows**, which it will: it is the
# same concept in the opposite direction and would want the same word, and
# label.rs's "each word appears at most once" rule would then silently drop
# one of them from a chain carrying both. Whoever adds てくる needs two words,
# not one.
#
# 未然形 and 連用形 are listed for the same reason 買っちゃわ is: the walk
# reaches them and every reachable tuple needs a row.
待っていけ	五段・タ行:連用タ接続 ていく:仮定形	Directional Conditional
待っていけ	五段・タ行:連用タ接続 ていく:命令ｅ	Directional Imperative
待っていきゃ	五段・タ行:連用タ接続 ていく:仮定縮約１	Directional Conditional
待っていく	五段・タ行:連用タ接続 ていく:基本形	Directional
待っていこ	五段・タ行:連用タ接続 ていく:未然ウ接続	Directional
待っていか	五段・タ行:連用タ接続 ていく:未然形	Directional
待っていっ	五段・タ行:連用タ接続 ていく:連用タ接続	Directional
待っていき	五段・タ行:連用タ接続 ていく:連用形	Directional
遊んでいけ	五段・バ行:連用タ接続 でいく:仮定形	Directional Conditional
遊んでいけ	五段・バ行:連用タ接続 でいく:命令ｅ	Directional Imperative
遊んでいきゃ	五段・バ行:連用タ接続 でいく:仮定縮約１	Directional Conditional
遊んでいく	五段・バ行:連用タ接続 でいく:基本形	Directional
遊んでいこ	五段・バ行:連用タ接続 でいく:未然ウ接続	Directional
遊んでいか	五段・バ行:連用タ接続 でいく:未然形	Directional
遊んでいっ	五段・バ行:連用タ接続 でいく:連用タ接続	Directional
遊んでいき	五段・バ行:連用タ接続 でいく:連用形	Directional
#
# てくる/でくる, ておく/でおく and てみる/でみる are the three 〜て auxiliaries
# the ていく note above names as still split, added 2026-09-21. Measured over
# four further visual-novel corpora, 75,782 sentences: of the literal windows
# in the text, the engine cut 2,368 of 3,232 〜てくる (73.3%), 223 of 241
# 〜ておく (92.5%) and 422 of 425 〜てみる (99.3%), hints on. 〜てくる alone is
# twice the rate 〜ていく was fixed at.
#
# カ変・クル is 来る's own class, 五段・カ行イ音便 is 置く's and 一段 is 見る's,
# so each pair needs one row per voicing plus the second attachment site the
# ていく note explains. でくる/でおく/でみる follow an onbin stem only.
#
# "Approaching", "Preparatory" and "Tentative" are the FOURTH, FIFTH and SIXTH
# words in this file the header's Wikipedia terminology list does not carry.
# Preparatory and Tentative are the standard grammatical terms for those two
# aspects and need no more defence than Completive did. Approaching is the one
# that was chosen rather than found: the note above reserved a second word for
# 〜てくる precisely because it is the same directional concept as 〜ていく in
# the opposite direction and label.rs would drop a repeat, so it cannot also be
# "Directional". It is plain English in this file's learner register rather
# than the linguists' "venitive", and the cost is that the pair no longer reads
# as a pair.
#
# **Three forms of てくる/でくる are blocked in AUX_FORM_BLOCK and so have no
# rows here**, which is why this block is shorter than the class's form list.
# カ変's 仮定形 is くれ, its 体言接続特殊 くん and its 体言接続特殊２ く, and in
# real text all three of those surfaces belong to something else: 〜てくれ is
# くれる, the giving auxiliary (2,455 occurrences against 7 of 〜てくれば),
# 〜てくん is its contraction, and 919 of the bare 〜てく are 〜てください. See
# table.rs for the ledger.
#
# 待っておいで (5 occurrences) can still merge as ておい + で and is left
# standing: too rare to buy a block of its own, and the shape is named here so
# that whoever meets it knows it was seen.

#
# てる/でる are the ている/でいる contraction, the colloquial progressive:
# 思ってる, 遊んでる, 食べてる. table.rs gives them their own ATTACHES_TO
# rows for the same reason ちゃう has them -- IPADIC tokenizes the
# contraction as its own token, and although JMdict does carry てる and
# でる as headwords, reaching that entry needs a separate span and the only
# span that could precede one is refused by the tokenizer constraint. See
# table.rs.
#
# "Progressive" is the SECOND word in this file that the Wikipedia
# terminology list in the header does not carry -- that article discusses
# ている under its gerund and infinitive sections and gives no one-word
# English gloss, and it uses "continuative" only as an alias for 連用形.
# Like Completive above, the word is the standard grammatical term for the
# aspect (Wikipedia, "Grammatical aspect", read 2026-09). The aspect is
# genuinely ambiguous -- progressive for 走ってる, resultative for
# 知ってる and 結婚してる -- but unlike れる/られる the two readings are not
# balanced, so the primary one is used unqualified, which is the Completive
# precedent rather than the Passive/Potential one. JMdict's own gloss for
# the entry is "to be ...-ing" and agrees.
#
# 未然形 and 連用形 are the empty-suffix stems, listed for the same reason
# 買っちゃわ is: the walk reaches them and every reachable tuple needs a row.

#
# The godan potential, added 2026-09-23 as table.rs's `る` row: 書け + る.
# IPADIC files 可能動詞 as 一段 lexemes of their own, so until then the table
# never reached the godan lemma and 書けた read 書け "Conditional" + た. The
# lemma is a bare る conjugating as 一段 over the godan's own 仮定形. Its
# 未然形 and 連用形 are empty, so they are zero-width steps the table takes
# only under a following auxiliary, and they have no depth-1 row for the
# reason a BOUND_FORMS form has no depth-0 row: neither is ever a word on its
# own. The rows after the first three are the chains that go through them.
#
# "Potential" is the SEVENTH word in this file that the header's Wikipedia
# list does not carry as written -- it carries "Passive/Potential", which is
# right for れる/られる and wrong here: 書ける cannot be a passive, so the
# slash would assert an ambiguity this form does not have.
#
# **Four of the potential's forms are blocked in AUX_FORM_BLOCK and so have no
# rows**: 命令ｙｏ and 未然ウ接続, both よ, because 待てよ is an imperative and
# the particle よ; 命令ｒｏ ろ, because the potential has no imperative; and
# 体言接続特殊 ん, which would tie with the negative 書けん below and win on
# depth, reading "can't write" as "can".
書ける	五段・カ行イ音便:仮定形 る:基本形	Potential
書けれ	五段・カ行イ音便:仮定形 る:仮定形	Potential Conditional
書けりゃ	五段・カ行イ音便:仮定形 る:仮定縮約１	Potential Conditional
書けた	五段・カ行イ音便:仮定形 る:連用形 た:基本形	Potential Past
書けない	五段・カ行イ音便:仮定形 る:未然形 ない:基本形	Potential Negative
書けなかった	五段・カ行イ音便:仮定形 る:未然形 ない:連用タ接続 た:基本形	Potential Negative Past
書けます	五段・カ行イ音便:仮定形 る:連用形 ます:基本形	Potential Polite
書けて	五段・カ行イ音便:仮定形 る:連用形 て:基本形	Potential Te-form
書けず	五段・カ行イ音便:仮定形 る:未然形 ぬ:連用ニ接続	Potential Negative
書けん	五段・カ行イ音便:仮定形 る:未然形 ん:基本形	Potential Negative
